options.text: Long night?
Quiet watch tonight?
Clear sky, at least. Good stars.
Cold enough to crack teeth tonight. How do you stand it?
How do you stay awake out here?
Want some company for a bit?
You seem jumpy tonight.
Dark comes early this season.
You on till dawn?
What do you miss most on nights like this?
Morning. Sleep any?
Sun's brutal today.
Slow day?
Good light for marching, at least.
Loud morning. Drills?
Made it through another night, then.
Had your breakfast yet?
Dust never settles around here, does it?
Even the birds sound tired today.
That was close.
Still standing, I see.
You hurt?
You fight well.
What just happened here?
Are they gone?
Think more are coming?
Does it get easier?
Your hands are shaking.
You won. That counts for something.
Rough one. Lose anyone?
Mind if I come through?
Just visiting. That allowed?
Can I look around?
Any rules I should know inside?
Is this a trading day?
Any chance of a bed tonight?
Solid walls. Your work?
Busy post today.
New faces on the gate. Rotation?
Feels safe in here. Rare thing.
Something smells good. Mess tent?
They drill you hard here?
How long have you been posted here?
What do you do between alarms?
Do you ever get home?
Think these walls would hold a real push?
The young ones look nervous.
They pay you enough for this?
That banner's flown through a lot, huh?
Anywhere quiet a traveler can sit a while?
Didn't expect anyone out here.
You startled me.
Long walk today?
How are the boots holding up?
Share a fire if you're stopping?
You're carrying heavy for a patrol.
Which way are you headed?
All quiet out here?
You all look dog-tired.
I'll just pass by, if that's fine.
We're a long way from any road.
You out here alone?
Hunting, or hiding?
Beautiful country, when nobody's fighting over it.
You look off your path.
My camp's close. You're welcome at the fire.
Quiet out here. No witnesses to anything.
What drags a soldier this deep into nowhere?
You look short on supplies.
Looks like we're walking the same direction.
So. Here we are again.
I'm not looking for another fight.
We can both walk away from this.
Your move, soldier.
For what it's worth, I didn't want it to go that way.
You're staring. Say it.
Are we even yet, or close?
Blades down. I just want to talk.
Next time might go differently.
You're out late.
Cold watch to draw, this far out.
See anything moving tonight?
No fire? Rough way to spend a night.
At least there's moonlight.
I nearly walked right into you in the dark.
Do you always walk the dark hours?
I'll sit up with you a while, if you want.
I heard wolves earlier. Close ones.
Need a hand with the wounded?
I have bandages, if you need them.
I can spare food and water.
I'll help carry, if someone's hurt.
Who attacked you?
I'll help you bury them, if it comes to that.
Rest. I'll keep watch a moment.
Want me to carry word to your people?
You look like you had it handled.
Storm's coming. You can smell it.
Three days of rain and counting.
That wind's been howling all day.
This heat could kill a man faster than any war.
Where do you shelter when the sky opens out here?
Early snow this year, isn't it?
That lightning's getting closer.
The mud's eating the trails whole.
Think the weather breaks soon?

negative: Long enough. Made longer by visitors.
The watch is fine. Watching you, mostly.
neutral: Every night is long. That's what makes them nights.
Awake? We traded sleep for seniority years ago.
The cold keeps the sentimental thoughts short. Useful.
positive: Long, cold, and quiet — my three favorite kinds of boring, friend.
Stars are good tonight. Somewhere someone's navigating by them toward us. Ha.
Sit. The thermos is engine-flavored but it's hot.

negative: Watch status is nominal. Your presence is the anomaly.
The night's under control. Stay where the light touches you.
neutral: All quiet on the net. Intend to keep it that way.
Shift runs to the dawn bell. Routine, if nothing changes it.
Alertness is a discipline, not a mood. So: fine.
positive: Quiet shift so far. Your voice is the loudest thing since sundown — pleasantly so.
On till first light, then hand over and sleep like the honored dead.
Company's welcome. Stand left of the lantern so I keep my night eyes.

negative: The night is long for those with debts. How is yours passing?
We do not sleep much. It is a professional advantage.
neutral: The night is a river. We stand in it and let it pass.
Cold, yes. The stars pay for their beauty with distance.
Awake is a habit. The desert teaches it with consequences.
positive: Sit, friend. The dark is kinder shared, and the kettle is nearly singing.
What do I miss? Rain on a tent roof. A very small music.
The stars are gossiping tonight. Stay; I will translate the good parts.

negative: The day is slow. My patience is slower. Don't race them.
Slept fine. One eye. The other watched for your sort.
neutral: Sun, dust, drill, repeat. The war's honest that way.
Sleep is rationed like everything else. We manage.
The birds are tired because they nest near artillery. Everyone adapts.
positive: Another dawn on the right side of the dirt. Small victory, counts double.
Breakfast was gray and heroic, like everything from our kitchens. Want some?
Slow day, good day. Excitement out here is always somebody's funeral.

negative: The day proceeds on schedule. You're the unscheduled part.
Rest cycles are adequate. Vigilance cycles are constant. Note that.
neutral: Morning drills, as scheduled. Noise means readiness.
Slow is the objective. Every quiet hour is a mission accomplished.
Conditions are hot but within operating tolerances.
positive: Slept four hours straight — practically a holiday. What brings you by?
Good marching light, agreed. The kind of morning that makes the maps look optimistic.
Mess is still serving. Tell them the gate sent you; the portions improve.

negative: The sun sees everything. Today it watches you especially.
Slow days sharpen knives. Ours are very sharp.
neutral: The heat is an old landlord. We pay it and it leaves us standing.
Dust is the desert breathing. You get used to the rhythm.
Morning came, as it insists on doing. We were awake to greet it.
positive: Another night survived is a debt the dawn repays, friend. Sit in the shade.
Breakfast was dates and bread. There are dates left, if your hands are quick.
Even tired birds sing. That is most of wisdom, honestly.

negative: Close for them. Closer for you, if you linger.
We're standing. Standing is the whole job. Move on.
neutral: Close is the only kind of call the line gets. We're used to the arithmetic.
Hurt? Bruises are receipts. We keep them filed.
They're gone. Gone has a habit of coming back with friends, so keep walking.
positive: Ha — you saw that? The line bends, the line snaps back. Good day for our side.
Shaking hands just mean the body did its bookkeeping. It passes, friend.
We lost nobody today. Say that word again slowly: nobody. Best word there is.

negative: Engagement concluded. Your proximity to it is being evaluated.
We're operational. That's all the report you're owed.
neutral: Contact resolved. Casualties minimal, posture restored.
Hostiles withdrew. Pursuit was outside our tasking.
Whether more come is a planning question. We plan for yes.
positive: Appreciate the concern. Clean engagement — textbook, honestly. The drills pay rent.
A scratch and a dented pauldron. The armorer will lecture me; I'll deserve it.
Does it get easier? The work, yes. The after — you learn where to put it.

negative: The fight ended as fights end. Do not stand where the next one starts.
We are whole. The ones who tested us are less so. Walk on.
neutral: Close, yes. The knife's whisper. We have heard it before.
They fled into the open ground. The open ground is on our side.
Wounds we bind. Names we remember. Both quietly.
positive: You watched us dance, friend. The desert taught the steps; we only follow.
My hands shake after, always. It is the body praying. Let it finish.
No graves today. Tonight the tea will taste like victory, which is to say: sweeter.

negative: The gate's for the line and its friends. Guess your column.
Through? No. Around. Far around.
neutral: Pass, but walk the marked path. The unmarked ones are marked differently, if you follow.
Trading's at the outer sheds. Inside stays inside.
Rules: touch nothing, salute nobody, leave by dark.
positive: Come through, friend. Wipe the boots — the mud inside is domesticated.
There's a bunk in the transit dugout if the night catches you. First come, first snoring.
Busy day, aye. Quota inspection. Everyone's suddenly very fond of shovels.

negative: Entry denied. Your file doesn't support access.
This installation is closed to you. The road, however, is open. Use it.
neutral: Escorted access only. Wait here; an escort will be assigned.
Visitors keep to the commerce lane. Deviation voids the welcome.
Trade day is posted on the board. Read the board, not my patience.
positive: Cleared through, friend. Check in at the shadow of the tower; they'll stamp you.
Guest billets have space tonight. Quartermaster's tent, mention the gate log.
Rotation just changed, hence the new faces. The standards rotated in with them.

negative: The camp's mouth is closed to you. It has tasted your name.
Guests are chosen. You were not.
neutral: Enter as a guest enters: slowly, visibly, and grateful.
The tents have eyes and the carpets have ears. Behave for both.
Come for trade? The market rug is by the well. Prices soften at dusk.
positive: The shade is yours, friend. Duck the rope line and mind the sleeping dog — he outranks us.
A bed, yes — the guest tent smells of cedar and old stories. Both are free.
Safe is the word, yes. Safety here is woven, not built. Tread softly on it.

negative: The kitchen's not for you. Neither is the curiosity.
Posted here long enough to smell trouble. It smells like you.
neutral: Two winters at this post. The walls and I have an understanding.
Between alarms we sleep, sharpen, and argue about soup. Rich inner lives.
Would the walls hold? The walls are the least of what holds.
positive: That smell is Thursday stew. It has bones in it. Whose, we don't ask. Joking. Mostly.
Home? The line is home. The other home writes letters and worries. Both are good.
The nervous young ones live longest, friend. Fear is free armor.

negative: Facility questions from flagged persons go in a special report. Congratulations.
Pay, morale, and defenses are internal matters. You're external.
neutral: Posting length is standard rotation. Long enough to know every bolt.
Downtime is maintenance time. Gear first, then people. That's the order.
Recruits look nervous because training works. Calm comes later, calibrated.
positive: Eight months on station. I could walk this perimeter blind — occasionally have.
The pay's fair and the pension's a rumor. We serve for the ledger's other column.
That banner's been through two sieges and a laundry accident. It stays up.

negative: You ask many small questions. Small questions build large suspicions.
What we do between alarms is prepare for people like you.
neutral: How long here? The camp moves. Home is the moving, not the here.
Between alarms we mend nets, tell lies about fish, and watch the horizon.
The banner is old, yes. Old banners have outlived their doubters.
positive: Sit by the loom tent, friend — quietest corner we have, and the weaver hums well.
Home visits come with the pilgrim moons. Twice a year the desert loosens its grip.
The nervous ones? We give them tea and night duty. The stars finish the training.

negative: Nobody expects us. That's the point. Hands easy.
We're headed wherever you aren't. Make that simple for us.
neutral: Long walk, short rations, standard day. Pass on the left.
Quiet so far. You're the loudest thing since the crows.
Heavy packs, aye. The line carries its house on its back like a sad snail.
positive: Ha, startled you? Good — means the boots still know their trade.
Boots are one march from retirement. Like half the section, honestly.
We stop at the creek if you're brewing something. Fair trade: fire for gossip.

negative: You're an unexpected contact on a planned route. Statistically interesting. Explain.
Heading and purpose. Yours, not ours.
neutral: Routine sweep, on schedule. You may pass once we've logged you.
All quiet, which is how the report will read if nothing changes in the next minute.
The load-out is standard for extended patrol. Everything has a checklist line.
positive: Tired, yes — third leg of a long loop. Your face is a welcome change from terrain.
We push northeast to the marker stone, then home. Walk the first stretch with us if you like.
Careful passing on the ridge side. Ground's loose. We nearly lost a boot and its officer.

negative: No one expects us. Yet here we are, and here you are. Curious arithmetic.
Where we walk is written nowhere. Where you walk is now noted.
neutral: The desert told us someone was ahead. It rarely bothers lying.
Quiet, yes. Quiet is a crop. We tend it.
We carry heavy because the land lends nothing and charges interest.
positive: Startled, friend? The sand walks softly and we are its students.
We drift toward the well country. Your direction and ours braid for a while — walk along.
Dog-tired is honest work's perfume. Tonight we sleep like buried kings.

negative: Far from roads, far from rules. Bad math for you, stranger.
No witnesses works both directions. Think hard.
neutral: Alone? The line is never alone. It just spreads out.
Scouting ground. Somebody has to know where the next trench goes.
Beautiful country, sure. Beauty out here is just danger resting.
positive: Deep nowhere, friend, aye — checking springs and counting deer. War fodder, all of it.
Short on supplies, long on stubbornness. The classic ratio. We'll manage.
Same direction, is it? Fine. You talk, I'll grunt. Division of labor.

negative: Remote contact, no witnesses, flagged individual. You see how this file reads. Behave.
Off-grid meetings with you are exactly what protocol warns about.
neutral: Solo reconnaissance. Sanctioned, mapped, and expected back. Note the last part.
Off my path? Negative. The path is classified; I'm precisely on it.
This far out, assistance is one signal flare away. For both our reference.
positive: Surveying ground for a future outpost. You're standing in tomorrow's mess hall, roughly.
I'd take the fire, friend. Cold rations lose their charm around day three.
Same heading? Good. Two sets of eyes halve the surprises.

negative: Alone is a word for people the desert has not adopted.
Deep nowhere is our parlor, guest. Mind the furniture.
neutral: Hunting, hiding — the desert rarely distinguishes. Neither do we.
The empty land is not empty. It is patient. Different thing.
My path is where my feet are. I am never off it.
positive: Your fire is a generous word, friend. I bring tea leaves and one truly excellent lie.
What drags me out here? The stars are cleaner where no one bleeds. I visit them.
We walk the same direction because the good water is that way. Wisdom travels in pairs.

vengeful: Here we are. You, me, and eleven reasons. Pick your next word like a last meal.
Even? The ledger has pages left. Pray we never finish the book.
negative: Again, yes. Every meeting we don't fight is a loan, not a gift.
Walk away, then. Slowly. The line's mercy has a speed limit.
Not looking for a fight. Found one before, though, didn't you.
neutral: Blades down, fine. The count between us stays open, but today can stay quiet.
You didn't want it that way. Wars are made of things nobody wanted. Go.
Next time, maybe. This time, walk. The mud's had enough to drink this week.
positive: The past between us is buried in a marked grave, friend. Leave flowers, not questions.
We're even enough that I'm talking, not counting. Keep it there.

vengeful: Your casualty record with this command is memorized. One motion decides the rest.
We are one breach from resolution. Choose stillness.
negative: De-escalation accepted, provisionally. Hands stay visible until you're a dot.
Walking away is approved. It's the only approved item on your list.
Your apology is noted for the record. The record is long.
neutral: Stand down mirrored. This contact stays administrative if you keep it there.
Even isn't a category we track. Contained is. You're currently contained.
Talk, then. Two meters of distance and no sudden anything.
positive: History acknowledged and shelved. You've balanced it since. Don't audit it again.
We've logged worse men into friends. Keep making that easy.

vengeful: The sand between us drinks slowly, killer. It is still swallowing what you spilled.
Speak softly. The graves you filled are listening with us.
negative: You wear our blood like a coat you forgot you stole. Walk away in it.
No fight today, then. The desert schedules these things better than men do.
Say your peace and step back from it. Some words need distance to cool.
neutral: We are not even. We are paused. There is grace in a pause; do not spend it all.
Your regret has a true sound. Keep it tuned. It may yet buy you shade.
Talk, traveler. The knives will nap, light sleepers though they are.
positive: What was between us the wind took, friend. Do not chase the wind to ask for it back.
The scales settled. Sit; scars make the oldest, best stories.

negative: Late for you. Working hours for us. State it and go.
The dark out here is ours by lease. Your visit isn't on it.
neutral: No fire, no target. Old trench wisdom, still undefeated.
Something's always moving at night. The trick is knowing what's allowed to.
Wolves, aye. They follow armies like gulls follow ships. Professional respect.
positive: Out late together, then. Sit on the cold side; the wind's rude tonight, friend.
Moonlight's a mixed ration — you see them, they see you. We take it anyway.
Sit up with me, sure. First one to fall asleep carries both packs tomorrow.

negative: Night movement near a patrol is how misunderstandings get names on them.
You found us in the dark. Consider how deliberate our finding you was.
neutral: Night operations are routine. Your being adjacent to one is not. Log it and move.
Negative contacts since dusk, present company now excepted.
No fire is doctrine, not hardship. Light discipline keeps rosters full.
positive: Nearly walked into me? Then the camouflage course finally paid off. Don't tell the instructor.
The dark hours rotate through everyone. Tonight's mine. The stars make it a fair trade.
Stay a while, friend. Quiet watch, good company — the report will say 'uneventful' and lie.

negative: The night is our workshop. Visitors handle nothing.
You walk loudly for someone so far from help.
neutral: We are always out late. Lateness is where our work lives.
Things move at night that respect us. Be one of them.
The wolves sang earlier, yes. We answered. It is polite.
positive: The moon lights the path for friends and the trap for others. You walk the lit part, friend.
No fire tonight — the dark is warm enough when it trusts you. Sit; it trusts you.
Sit up with me and I will show you which stars are lying about the way north.

negative: Our wounded are ours to carry. Your help would cost more than it lifts.
Keep your bandages. The line stitches itself.
neutral: The hurt are seen to. But water — water we'd take without ceremony.
Who attacked? The usual arithmetic in unusual boots. Details travel up, not out.
We bury our own, with our own shovels. It's the one ritual we're rich in.
positive: A hand with the stretchers? Take the left pole and match my step, friend.
Bandages accepted with honors. The medic will kiss you. Fair warning: mustache.
Watch a moment while we breathe? That's a comrade's offer. The line accepts.

negative: Casualty handling is internal. Unverified aid is a vector, not a kindness.
Step back from the wounded. Assistance requires clearance you lack.
neutral: Medical response is en route. Your offer is noted and logged as goodwill.
Attacker identification is pending review. No comment before the review.
If you're carrying clean water, that we'll accept. Standard containers only.
positive: Yes — pressure on that wound, right there, while I splint. Good hands. Thank you.
Carry word to the crossroads post: two litters inbound, one urgent. Run it, friend.
Your supplies just shortened a bad day. Aegis logs its debts in permanent ink.

negative: Our blood is not a stranger's business. Walk wide of it.
The wounded have kin. You are not kin. It is that simple tonight.
neutral: The hurt are already in gentler hands than ours. But your offer is heard.
Who struck us? The answer is being prepared. It will be delivered personally.
If it comes to graves, the sand digs easily here. We will manage the rest.
positive: Bring your bandages and sit by the fire, friend. Healing likes witnesses.
Pour the water slowly for him — small sips, like rain teaching a seed.
Rest, you say, and you will watch? Then I will rest. That is a gift with weight.

negative: Storm's coming, and you're between me and shelter. Fix one of those.
Weather talk. From you. The rain's more sincere.
neutral: Rain, mud, wind — the war's oldest veterans. They never rotate out.
We shelter where the ground says so. The ground is rarely generous.
It breaks when it breaks. Weather and sieges, same rules.
positive: Smell it? That's a two-shovel storm, friend. Dig in with us; misery scales well.
Early snow means short campaigning. Best news the sky's sent all year.
The mud eats trails, boots, and morale, in that order. We're negotiating.

negative: Weather's inbound and my patience is outbound. Conclude your business.
Storm cover is for personnel. You're weather-exposed by status.
neutral: Forecast says the front passes by morning. Plan movement after, not during.
Lightning protocol is simple: low ground, no metal, no heroics.
The heat's within tolerances. Hydration discipline handles the rest.
positive: Storm shelter's the overhang past the twin firs. Room for one more, friend.
Three days of rain means three days of cleaning gear. Morale survives on grumbling.
The wind's stripping our signal flags bald. Requisition will love that memo.

negative: The storm and I have an arrangement. You are not included in it.
The sky opens for everyone. Shelter opens for fewer.
neutral: When the sky opens we fold into the rocks, like the land's own thought.
The wind howls because it remembers. Let it. Memory passes.
Heat kills the hurried. Walk slow, drink small, arrive alive.
positive: Come under the lee of the dune, friend. The storm is a guest too; we will host it together.
Lightning close, yes — the sky sharpening its spears. We are too small for its war. Sit.
The weather breaks when the desert finishes speaking. It is nearly done; I know the cadence.
